page: Microsoft Azure L4s_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance from the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, including AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a 960 GB drive and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2158.0 and a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.48 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is weak at 3990.37, and the uncached memory bandwidth read-only large block speed is also weak at 36.35 GB/sec. Database operations, such as Redis SET operations, register at a weak 5.68 million operations per second, while Passmark database operations score an average 2891.14. Small-model LLM inference achieves average speeds of 515.22 tokens per second for prompt processing, but performance drops to a poor 4.52 tokens per second for text generation on medium models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L4s_v4 offers a high local storage capacity of 960 GB and a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, making it a dense resource option for storage-centric workloads without the overhead of larger instance classes. However, the tradeoff lies in its weak multi-core scaling and limited memory bandwidth. This server is suited for single-threaded tasks, text processing, local database caching, and lightweight web serving, but is less optimal for multi-threaded compilation or larger language model inference.
